Haitian Vodou.fact: Agwe rules the sea with his consort, La Sirène.

Haitian Vodou.subject: Women & Society
Haitian Vodou.question: She is a mermaid, and is sometimes described as Èzili of the _____ because she brings good luck and wealth from the sea
Haitian Vodou.fact: She is a mermaid, and is sometimes described as Èzili of the Waters because she brings good luck and wealth from the sea.

Haitian Vodou.subject: Women & Society
Haitian Vodou.question: Also bearing the name Èzili is Èzili Freda or _____, the lwa of love and luxury who personifies feminine beauty and grace, and Ezili Dantor, who takes the form of a peasant woman
Haitian Vodou.fact: Also bearing the name Èzili is Èzili Freda or Erzuli Freda, the lwa of love and luxury who personifies feminine beauty and grace, and Ezili Dantor, who takes the form of a peasant woman.

Haitian Vodou.subject: Women & Society
Haitian Vodou.question: Azaka is the lwa of crops and agriculture, usually addressed as "Papa" or "_____"
Haitian Vodou.fact: Azaka is the lwa of crops and agriculture, usually addressed as "Papa" or "Cousin".

Haitian Vodou.subject: Women & Society
Haitian Vodou.question: His consort is the female lwa _____
Haitian Vodou.fact: His consort is the female lwa Kouzinn.

Haitian Vodou.subject: Women & Society
Haitian Vodou.question: Sogbo is a lwa associated with lightning, while his companion, _____, is associated with the wind
Haitian Vodou.fact: Sogbo is a lwa associated with lightning, while his companion, Bade, is associated with the wind.

Haitian Vodou.subject: Women & Society
Haitian Vodou.question: Danbala and his consort _____-Weddo are often depicted as a pair of intertwining snakes
Haitian Vodou.fact: Danbala and his consort Ayida-Weddo are often depicted as a pair of intertwining snakes.

Haitian Vodou.subject: Women & Society
Haitian Vodou.question: Guarding fountains and marshes are spirits called the _____
Haitian Vodou.fact: Guarding fountains and marshes are spirits called the Simbi.

Haitian Vodou.subject: Women & Society
Haitian Vodou.question: Usually seen as a fanmi rather than a nanchon, the _____ are associated with the realm of the dead
Haitian Vodou.fact: Usually seen as a fanmi rather than a nanchon, the Gede are associated with the realm of the dead. His consort is Gran Brigit, who has authority over cemeteries and is mother to many of the other Gede.

Haitian Vodou.subject: Women & Society
Haitian Vodou.question: The head of the family is _____ ("Baron Saturday"); he is associated with the phallus, the skull, and the graveyard cross, the latter used to highlight his presence in a Haitian cemetery
Haitian Vodou.fact: The head of the family is Baron Samedi ("Baron Saturday"); he is associated with the phallus, the skull, and the graveyard cross, the latter used to highlight his presence in a Haitian cemetery.

Haitian Vodou.subject: Women & Society
Haitian Vodou.question: His consort is _____, who has authority over cemeteries and is mother to many of the other Gede
Haitian Vodou.fact: His consort is Gran Brigit, who has authority over cemeteries and is mother to many of the other Gede.

Haitian Vodou.subject: Women & Society
Haitian Vodou.question: These particular links rely on analogies between the respective functions of these figures; Azaka, the lwa of agriculture, is for instance associated with _____ the farmer
Haitian Vodou.fact: These particular links rely on analogies between the respective functions of these figures; Azaka, the lwa of agriculture, is for instance associated with Saint Isidore the farmer.

Haitian Vodou.subject: Women & Society
Haitian Vodou.question: Similarly, as the "key" to the spirit world, _____ is typically associated with Saint Peter, who traditionally holds keys in Roman Catholic imagery
Haitian Vodou.fact: Similarly, as the "key" to the spirit world, Papa Legba is typically associated with Saint Peter, who traditionally holds keys in Roman Catholic imagery.

Haitian Vodou.subject: Women & Society
Haitian Vodou.question: The lwa of love and luxury, Èzili Freda, is associated with _____
Haitian Vodou.fact: The lwa of love and luxury, Èzili Freda, is associated with Mater Dolorosa.

Haitian Vodou.subject: Women & Society
Haitian Vodou.question: Danbala the serpent is often equated with _____, who is traditionally depicted with snakes, or with Moses, whose staff turned into serpents according to the Book of Exodus
Haitian Vodou.fact: Danbala the serpent is often equated with Saint Patrick, who is traditionally depicted with snakes, or with Moses, whose staff turned into serpents according to the Book of Exodus.

Haitian Vodou.subject: Women & Society
Haitian Vodou.question: The Marasa, or sacred twins, are typically equated with the twin saints _____ and Damian
Haitian Vodou.fact: The Marasa, or sacred twins, are typically equated with the twin saints Cosmas and Damian.

Haitian Vodou.subject: Women & Society
Haitian Vodou.question: Vodouists may originally have adopted the _____ saints to conceal lwa worship when the latter was illegal during the colonial period
Haitian Vodou.fact: Vodouists may originally have adopted the Roman Catholic saints to conceal lwa worship when the latter was illegal during the colonial period. However, by at least the late 20th century, many Vodouists expressed genuine devotion to the Roman Catholic saints, with the scholar Marc A. Christophe stating that most modern Vodouists genuinely see the saints and lwa as one, reflecting Vodou's "all-inclusive and harmonizing characteristics".

Haitian Vodou.subject: Women & Society
Haitian Vodou.question: Vodouists also often adopt and reinterpret biblical stories and theorise about the nature of Jesus of _____
Haitian Vodou.fact: Vodouists also often adopt and reinterpret biblical stories and theorise about the nature of Jesus of Nazareth.

Haitian Vodou.subject: Women & Society
Haitian Vodou.question: Vodou holds that _____ has preordained the time of everyone's death
Haitian Vodou.fact: Vodou holds that Bondye has preordained the time of everyone's death. It does not teach the existence of an afterlife realm akin to the Christian heaven and hell; instead, a common belief is that at bodily death, the gwo bonnanj join the Ginen, or ancestral spirits, while the ti bonnanj faces judgement before Bondye.

Haitian Vodou.subject: Women & Society
Haitian Vodou.question: The land of the _____ is often identified as being beneath the sea, under the earth, or above the sky
Haitian Vodou.fact: It does not teach the existence of an afterlife realm akin to the Christian heaven and hell; instead, a common belief is that at bodily death, the gwo bonnanj join the Ginen, or ancestral spirits, while the ti bonnanj faces judgement before Bondye. The land of the Ginen is often identified as being beneath the sea, under the earth, or above the sky.

Haitian Vodou.subject: Women & Society
Haitian Vodou.question: The term is quite flexible; maji is usually used to denigrate other _____, although some practitioners employ it as a self-descriptor for Petwo rites
Haitian Vodou.fact: The term is quite flexible; maji is usually used to denigrate other Vodouists, although some practitioners employ it as a self-descriptor for Petwo rites. This view of destiny has been interpreted as encouraging a fatalistic outlook, something that the religion's critics, especially from Christian backgrounds, argue discourages Vodouists from improving their society.

Haitian Vodou.subject: Women & Society
Haitian Vodou.question: This has been extended into an argument that Vodou is responsible for Haiti's poverty, a view that has been accused of being rooted in _____ colonial prejudices towards Africans
Haitian Vodou.fact: This has been extended into an argument that Vodou is responsible for Haiti's poverty, a view that has been accused of being rooted in European colonial prejudices towards Africans.

Haitian Vodou.subject: Women & Society
Haitian Vodou.question: Some Vodouists argue that the lwa determine a person's sexual orientation, while forms of Èzili are seen as the patron of masisi (gay men), and Èzili _____ò is sometimes regarded as a lesbian
Haitian Vodou.fact: Some Vodouists argue that the lwa determine a person's sexual orientation, while forms of Èzili are seen as the patron of masisi (gay men), and Èzili Dantò is sometimes regarded as a lesbian.

Haitian Vodou.subject: Women & Society
Haitian Vodou.question: Ceremonies for a particular lwa often coincide with the feast day of the _____ saint which that lwa is associated with
Haitian Vodou.fact: Ceremonies for a particular lwa often coincide with the feast day of the Roman Catholic saint which that lwa is associated with.

Haitian Vodou.subject: Women & Society
Haitian Vodou.question: Oungan numerically dominate in rural _____, while there is a more equitable balance of priests and priestesses in urban areas
Haitian Vodou.fact: Unlike in Santería and Candomblé, which employ Yoruba as a liturgical language not understood by most practitioners, in Vodou the liturgies are predominantly in Haitian Creole, the everyday language of most Vodouists. Oungan numerically dominate in rural Haiti, while there is a more equitable balance of priests and priestesses in urban areas.

Haitian Vodou.subject: Women & Society
Haitian Vodou.question: As a result, "temple Vodou" is now more common in rural areas of _____ than it was in historical periods
Haitian Vodou.fact: As a result, "temple Vodou" is now more common in rural areas of Haiti than it was in historical periods.

Haitian Vodou.subject: Women & Society
Haitian Vodou.question: Vodouists believe that the oungan's role is modelled on the lwa Loco; in Vodou mythology, he was the first oungan and his consort _____ the first manbo
Haitian Vodou.fact: Vodouists believe that the oungan's role is modelled on the lwa Loco; in Vodou mythology, he was the first oungan and his consort Ayizan the first manbo.

Haitian Vodou.subject: Women & Society
Haitian Vodou.question: The oungan and manbo are expected to display the power of second sight, something regarded as a gift from _____ that can be revealed to the individual through visions or dreams
Haitian Vodou.fact: The oungan and manbo are expected to display the power of second sight, something regarded as a gift from Bondye that can be revealed to the individual through visions or dreams.

Haitian Vodou.subject: Women & Society
Haitian Vodou.question: An alternative term is gangan, although the connotations of this term vary regionally in _____
Haitian Vodou.fact: An alternative term is gangan, although the connotations of this term vary regionally in Haiti.

Haitian Vodou.subject: Women & Society
Haitian Vodou.question: The size and shape of ounfòs vary, from basic shacks to more lavish structures, the latter being more common in Port-au-_____
Haitian Vodou.fact: The size and shape of ounfòs vary, from basic shacks to more lavish structures, the latter being more common in Port-au-Prince.

Haitian Vodou.subject: Women & Society
Haitian Vodou.question: However, in the Haitian diaspora many _____ perform their rites in basements, where no poto mitan are available
Haitian Vodou.fact: However, in the Haitian diaspora many Vodouists perform their rites in basements, where no poto mitan are available.

Haitian Vodou.subject: Women & Society
Haitian Vodou.question: Also present may be a sink dedicated to the lwa _____-Wedo
Haitian Vodou.fact: Also present may be a sink dedicated to the lwa Danbala-Wedo.

Haitian Vodou.subject: Women & Society
Haitian Vodou.question: Every ounfò usually has a room or corner of a room devoted to _____
Haitian Vodou.fact: Every ounfò usually has a room or corner of a room devoted to Erzuli Freda.

Haitian Vodou.subject: Women & Society
Haitian Vodou.question: The area around the ounfò often contains objects dedicated to particular lwa, such as a pool of water for Danbala, a black cross for _____, and a pince (iron bar) embedded in a brazier for Criminel
Haitian Vodou.fact: The area around the ounfò often contains objects dedicated to particular lwa, such as a pool of water for Danbala, a black cross for Baron Samedi, and a pince (iron bar) embedded in a brazier for Criminel.

Haitian Vodou.subject: Women & Society
Haitian Vodou.question: Finally, after the kouche, the new initiate may be expected to visit a _____ church
Haitian Vodou.fact: Finally, after the kouche, the new initiate may be expected to visit a Catholic church. An altar, or pè, will often contain images (typically lithographs) of Roman Catholic saints.

Haitian Vodou.subject: Women & Society
Haitian Vodou.question: Votive objects used in _____ are typically made from industrial materials, including iron, plastic, sequins, china, tinsel, and plaster
Haitian Vodou.fact: Votive objects used in Haiti are typically made from industrial materials, including iron, plastic, sequins, china, tinsel, and plaster.

Haitian Vodou.subject: Women & Society
Haitian Vodou.question: An altar, or pè, will often contain images (typically lithographs) of _____ saints
Haitian Vodou.fact: An altar, or pè, will often contain images (typically lithographs) of Roman Catholic saints. Since developing in the mid-19th century, chromolithography has also had an impact on Vodou imagery, facilitating the widespread availability of images of the Roman Catholic saints who are equated with the lwa.

Haitian Vodou.subject: Women & Society
Haitian Vodou.question: Cosentino encountered a shrine in Port-au-Prince where _____ was represented by a plastic statue of Santa Claus wearing a black sombrero, and in another by a statue of Star Wars-character Darth Vader
Haitian Vodou.fact: Cosentino encountered a shrine in Port-au-Prince where Baron Samedi was represented by a plastic statue of Santa Claus wearing a black sombrero, and in another by a statue of Star Wars-character Darth Vader.

Haitian Vodou.subject: Women & Society
Haitian Vodou.question: In ounfòs where both _____ and Petwo deities are worshipped, their altars are kept separate
Haitian Vodou.fact: In ounfòs where both Rada and Petwo deities are worshipped, their altars are kept separate.

Haitian Vodou.subject: Women & Society
Haitian Vodou.question: In rural _____, cemeteries are often family owned and play a key role in family rituals
Haitian Vodou.fact: In rural Haiti, cemeteries are often family owned and play a key role in family rituals.

Haitian Vodou.subject: Women & Society
Haitian Vodou.question: Other spaces used for Vodou rituals include _____ churches, rivers, the sea, fields, and markets
Haitian Vodou.fact: Other spaces used for Vodou rituals include Christian churches, rivers, the sea, fields, and markets.

Haitian Vodou.subject: Women & Society
Haitian Vodou.question: Different species of tree are associated with different lwa; Oyu, for example, is linked with mango trees, and _____ with bougainvillea
Haitian Vodou.fact: Different species of tree are associated with different lwa; Oyu, for example, is linked with mango trees, and Danbala with bougainvillea.

Haitian Vodou.subject: Women & Society
Haitian Vodou.question: Selected trees in _____ have had metal items affixed to them, serving as shrines to Ogou, who is associated with both iron and the roads
Haitian Vodou.fact: Selected trees in Haiti have had metal items affixed to them, serving as shrines to Ogou, who is associated with both iron and the roads.

Haitian Vodou.subject: Women & Society
Haitian Vodou.question: Spaces for ritual also appear in the homes of many _____, namely as a home altar called a wogatwa
Haitian Vodou.fact: Spaces for ritual also appear in the homes of many Vodouists, namely as a home altar called a wogatwa.

Haitian Vodou.subject: Women & Society
Haitian Vodou.question: The ason is a sacred rattle used in summoning the lwa, especially for _____ rites
Haitian Vodou.fact: The ason is a sacred rattle used in summoning the lwa, especially for Rada rites.

Haitian Vodou.subject: Women & Society
Haitian Vodou.question: Danbala for instance requires white foods, especially eggs, while _____'s offerings, whether meat, tubers, or vegetables, need to be grilled on a fire
Haitian Vodou.fact: Danbala for instance requires white foods, especially eggs, while Legba's offerings, whether meat, tubers, or vegetables, need to be grilled on a fire.

Haitian Vodou.subject: Women & Society
Haitian Vodou.question: The lwa of the Ogu and Nago nations prefer raw rum or clairin, while the lwa _____ avoids alcohol
Haitian Vodou.fact: The lwa of the Ogu and Nago nations prefer raw rum or clairin, while the lwa Ayizan avoids alcohol.

Haitian Vodou.subject: Women & Society
Haitian Vodou.question: Species used for sacrifice include chickens, goats, and bulls, with pigs often favored for _____ lwa
Haitian Vodou.fact: Species used for sacrifice include chickens, goats, and bulls, with pigs often favored for Petwo lwa.

Haitian Vodou.subject: Women & Society
Haitian Vodou.question: In the case of Agwé, a lwa of the sea, a white sheep may be sailed out to _____ and thrown overboard as a sacrifice
Haitian Vodou.fact: In the case of Agwé, a lwa of the sea, a white sheep may be sailed out to Trois Ilets and thrown overboard as a sacrifice.

Haitian Vodou.subject: Women & Society
Haitian Vodou.question: The ritual often begins with _____ prayers and hymns; these may be led by the prèt savann, although not all ounfò have anyone in this role
Haitian Vodou.fact: The ritual often begins with Roman Catholic prayers and hymns; these may be led by the prèt savann, although not all ounfò have anyone in this role.

Haitian Vodou.subject: Women & Society
Haitian Vodou.question: Two Haitian Creole songs, the Priyè Deyò ("_____"), may then be sung, lasting from 45 minutes to an hour
Haitian Vodou.fact: Two Haitian Creole songs, the Priyè Deyò ("Outside Prayers"), may then be sung, lasting from 45 minutes to an hour.

Haitian Vodou.subject: Women & Society
Haitian Vodou.question: Reflecting its status, when _____ enter the peristil they customarily bow before the drums
Haitian Vodou.fact: Vodouists believe that ritual drums contain an etheric force, the nanm, and a spirit called ountò. Reflecting its status, when Vodouists enter the peristil they customarily bow before the drums.

Haitian Vodou.subject: Women & Society
Haitian Vodou.question: Different types of drum are used, sometimes reserved for rituals devoted to specific lwa; _____ rites for instance involve two types of drum, whereas Rada rituals require three
Haitian Vodou.fact: Different types of drum are used, sometimes reserved for rituals devoted to specific lwa; Petwo rites for instance involve two types of drum, whereas Rada rituals require three.

Haitian Vodou.subject: Women & Society
Haitian Vodou.question: Drumming is typically accompanied by singing, usually in _____, although sometimes in Fon or Yoruba
Haitian Vodou.fact: Drumming is typically accompanied by singing, usually in Haitian Creole, although sometimes in Fon or Yoruba.

Haitian Vodou.subject: Women & Society
Haitian Vodou.question: Specific dance movements can indicate the lwa or their nanchon being summoned; dances for _____ for instance imitate swimming motions
Haitian Vodou.fact: Specific dance movements can indicate the lwa or their nanchon being summoned; dances for Agwe for instance imitate swimming motions.

Haitian Vodou.subject: Women & Society
Haitian Vodou.question: As their consciousness has been removed from their head during the possession, _____ believe that the chwal will have no memory of the incident
Haitian Vodou.fact: Vodouists believe that the lwa enters the head of the chwal and displaces their gwo bon anj, making the chwal tremble and convulse. As their consciousness has been removed from their head during the possession, Vodouists believe that the chwal will have no memory of the incident.

Haitian Vodou.subject: Women & Society
Haitian Vodou.question: These costumes and props help the chwal take on the appearance of the lwa; many ounfò have a large wooden phallus used by those possessed by _____ lwa, for instance
Haitian Vodou.fact: These costumes and props help the chwal take on the appearance of the lwa; many ounfò have a large wooden phallus used by those possessed by Gede lwa, for instance.

Haitian Vodou.subject: Women & Society
Haitian Vodou.question: Those believing themselves possessed by the serpent _____, for instance, often slither on the floor, dart out their tongue, and climb the posts of the peristil
Haitian Vodou.fact: Those believing themselves possessed by the serpent Danbala, for instance, often slither on the floor, dart out their tongue, and climb the posts of the peristil.

Haitian Vodou.subject: Women & Society
Haitian Vodou.question: Those possessed by _____, lwa of agriculture, will dress as a peasant in a straw hat with a clay pipe and will often speak in a rustic accent
Haitian Vodou.fact: Those possessed by Zaka, lwa of agriculture, will dress as a peasant in a straw hat with a clay pipe and will often speak in a rustic accent.

Haitian Vodou.subject: Women & Society
Haitian Vodou.question: Other forms of divination used by _____ include the casting of shells, cartomancy, studying leaves, coffee grounds or cinders in a glass, or looking into a candle flame
Haitian Vodou.fact: Other forms of divination used by Vodouists include the casting of shells, cartomancy, studying leaves, coffee grounds or cinders in a glass, or looking into a candle flame.

Haitian Vodou.subject: Women & Society
Haitian Vodou.question: A form of divination associated especially with _____ lwa is the use of a gembo shell, sometimes with a mirror attached to one side and affixed at both ends to string
Haitian Vodou.fact: A form of divination associated especially with Petwo lwa is the use of a gembo shell, sometimes with a mirror attached to one side and affixed at both ends to string.

Haitian Vodou.subject: Women & Society
Haitian Vodou.question: The latter term highlights the potential influence of the _____ minkisi on these Haitian ritual creations
Haitian Vodou.fact: The latter term highlights the potential influence of the Bakongo minkisi on these Haitian ritual creations.

Haitian Vodou.subject: Women & Society
Haitian Vodou.question: As the good lwa have rejected them as unworthy, bòko are believed to work with lwa achte ("bought lwa"), spirits that will work for anyone who pays them, and often members of the _____ nanchon
Haitian Vodou.fact: As the good lwa have rejected them as unworthy, bòko are believed to work with lwa achte ("bought lwa"), spirits that will work for anyone who pays them, and often members of the Petwo nanchon.

Haitian Vodou.subject: Women & Society
Haitian Vodou.question: The body is then buried in the cemetery, often according to _____ custom
Haitian Vodou.fact: The body is then buried in the cemetery, often according to Roman Catholic custom.

Haitian Vodou.subject: Women & Society
Haitian Vodou.question: In northern _____, an additional rite takes place at the ounfò on the day of the funeral, the kase kanari (breaking of the clay pot)
Haitian Vodou.fact: In northern Haiti, an additional rite takes place at the ounfò on the day of the funeral, the kase kanari (breaking of the clay pot).

Haitian Vodou.subject: Women & Society
Haitian Vodou.question: The night after the funeral, the novena takes place at the home of the deceased, involving _____ prayers; a mass for them is held a year after death, sometimes performed by a prèt savann
Haitian Vodou.fact: The night after the funeral, the novena takes place at the home of the deceased, involving Roman Catholic prayers; a mass for them is held a year after death, sometimes performed by a prèt savann.

Haitian Vodou.subject: Women & Society
Haitian Vodou.question: Many Vodouists believe that a practitioner's spirit dwells in the land of _____, located at the bottom of a lake or river, for a year and a day
Haitian Vodou.fact: Many Vodouists believe that a practitioner's spirit dwells in the land of Ginen, located at the bottom of a lake or river, for a year and a day.

Haitian Vodou.subject: Women & Society
Haitian Vodou.question: The notion of a spirit being encased in a vessel and then used for workings likely derives from _____ influences, and has similarities with the Bakongo-derived Palo religion from Cuba
Haitian Vodou.fact: The notion of a spirit being encased in a vessel and then used for workings likely derives from Bakongo influences, and has similarities with the Bakongo-derived Palo religion from Cuba.

Haitian Vodou.subject: Women & Society
Haitian Vodou.question: The practice is often linked to _____èl (secret societies), which are suspected of murdering the individual they wish to turn into a zonbi
Haitian Vodou.fact: The practice is often linked to Chanpwèl (secret societies), which are suspected of murdering the individual they wish to turn into a zonbi.

Haitian Vodou.subject: Women & Society
Haitian Vodou.question: Those intending to take a gwo bonnanj as a zonbi may have to borrow or buy them from _____
Haitian Vodou.fact: Those intending to take a gwo bonnanj as a zonbi may have to borrow or buy them from Baron Samedi.

Haitian Vodou.subject: Women & Society
Haitian Vodou.question: Devotions to the Gede are particularly common around the days of the dead, _____ (1 November) and All Souls (2 November), with celebrations largely taking place in the cemeteries of Port-au-Prince
Haitian Vodou.fact: Devotions to the Gede are particularly common around the days of the dead, All Saints (1 November) and All Souls (2 November), with celebrations largely taking place in the cemeteries of Port-au-Prince.

Haitian Vodou.subject: Women & Society
Haitian Vodou.question: At this festival, those devoted to the _____ dress in black and purple, with funeral frock coats, black veils, and top hats, all linking to the Gede's associations with death
Haitian Vodou.fact: Devotions to the Gede are particularly common around the days of the dead, All Saints (1 November) and All Souls (2 November), with celebrations largely taking place in the cemeteries of Port-au-Prince. At this festival, those devoted to the Gede dress in black and purple, with funeral frock coats, black veils, and top hats, all linking to the Gede's associations with death.

Haitian Vodou.subject: Women & Society
Haitian Vodou.question: The build-up to _____ sees Rara bands, largely consisting of peasants and the urban poor, process through the streets singing and dancing
Haitian Vodou.fact: The build-up to Easter sees Rara bands, largely consisting of peasants and the urban poor, process through the streets singing and dancing.

Haitian Vodou.subject: Women & Society
Haitian Vodou.question: Performing _____ is regarded as a service to the lwa, and some Rara leaders claim that a lwa instructed them to form their band
Haitian Vodou.fact: The build-up to Easter sees Rara bands, largely consisting of peasants and the urban poor, process through the streets singing and dancing. Each Rara band is considered to be under the patronage of a particular lwa, holding a contract with them that typically lasts seven years.

Haitian Vodou.subject: Women & Society
Haitian Vodou.question: They may also attempt to curse or poison rival _____ bands
Haitian Vodou.fact: Each Rara band is considered to be under the patronage of a particular lwa, holding a contract with them that typically lasts seven years. Performing Rara is regarded as a service to the lwa, and some Rara leaders claim that a lwa instructed them to form their band.

Haitian Vodou.subject: Women & Society
Haitian Vodou.question: In July, _____ pilgrims visit Plaine du Nord near Bwa Caiman, where according to legend the Haitian Revolution began
Haitian Vodou.fact: In July, Vodouist pilgrims visit Plaine du Nord near Bwa Caiman, where according to legend the Haitian Revolution began.

Haitian Vodou.subject: Women & Society
Haitian Vodou.question: The pilgrims gather before the Church of _____; Saint Jacques represents the lwa Ogou
Haitian Vodou.fact: The pilgrims gather before the Church of Saint Jacques; Saint Jacques represents the lwa Ogou.

Haitian Vodou.subject: Women & Society
Haitian Vodou.question: At the site, pilgrims bathe under waterfalls associated with water-spirits like _____
Haitian Vodou.fact: At the site, pilgrims bathe under waterfalls associated with water-spirits like Danbala.

Haitian Vodou.subject: Women & Society
Haitian Vodou.question: Haitian pilgrims commonly wear coloured ropes around their head or waist; a tradition that may derive from a _____ custom, kanga ("to tie"), during which sacred objects were bound with rope
Haitian Vodou.fact: Haitian pilgrims commonly wear coloured ropes around their head or waist; a tradition that may derive from a Bakongo custom, kanga ("to tie"), during which sacred objects were bound with rope.

Haitian Vodou.subject: Women & Society
Haitian Vodou.question: After the island's Taíno population was decimated, European colonists began importing West African slaves as a source of labor circa _____
Haitian Vodou.fact: After the island's Taíno population was decimated, European colonists began importing West African slaves as a source of labor circa 1512.
